title: What are ninja?
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the history and myths of ninja, starting with the claim that ninja trace roots to Chinese military thinking in Sun Tzu's Art of War, then legendary early figures like Prince Yamato and the 13-year-old Kumawaka avenging his father. They cover the true birthplace in the Iga and Koga regions, where clans sold ninja services as mercenaries; ninja castle-infiltration tales; anti-ninja defenses like squeaky nightingale floors and noisy bell-bottom garments; supernatural legends and the outhouse assassination story; ninja clothing (shinobi shozoku), weapons and gadgets such as tiger claws, caltrops, shuriken, water-walking shoes and collapsible boats; ninja in pop culture from James Bond's You Only Live Twice to G.I. Joe's Snake Eyes and Storm Shadow; and the Iga Ninja Museum festival. The episode ends with listener mail about geocaching and Santana CDs and a fan-made podcast inspired by the show.

segments.title: Opening banter and ninja pronunciation
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck joke about Josh's childhood ninja training with a neighborhood kid and make light of how to pronounce 'ninja'.

segments.title: Sun Tzu's Art of War and ninja roots
segments.summary: The hosts describe ninja as an art of war drawing on Sun Tzu's Art of War, which favored deception, sabotage, and espionage over the face-to-face samurai code of Bushido.

segments.title: Legendary early ninja: Prince Yamato and Kumawaka
segments.summary: They recount legendary early figures often called the first ninja: Prince Yamato, who disguised himself as a woman to kill barbarian chieftains, and a thirteen-year-old named Kumawaka who avenged his father by killing a monk using a moth trick and escaping over bamboo.

segments.title: Iga and Koga: the true birthplace of ninja
segments.summary: The hosts identify Iga and Koga as the regions where clans of ninja farmed themselves out as mercenaries to feudal lords, passing the craft from father to son, with ninja specializing in castle infiltration.

segments.title: Ninja legends, outhouse story and anti-ninja defenses
segments.summary: Stories of ninja tricks such as the flag theft and the lantern badge, the unverified outhouse assassination, and the defenses daimyo built, including noisy bell-bottom garments and squeaky nightingale floors.

segments.title: Supernatural ninja myths
segments.summary: The hosts discuss legends crediting ninja with superhuman powers such as flight, invisibility and walking through walls, and explain how these likely arose from their secrecy.

segments.title: Ninja clothing, weapons and gadgets
segments.summary: The hosts describe the black ninja uniform, the short sword, tiger claws, cow tongue-like caltrops, the water-walking shoes and collapsible boat, and note that the MythBusters tested and refuted some claims. They also say shuriken were mainly distracting weapons.

segments.title: Ninja in pop culture: movies, Ninja Turtles and G.I. Joe
segments.summary: The hosts discuss ninja in film, from You Only Live Twice onward, and in G.I. Joe, where Snake Eyes and Storm Shadow were once brothers in arms from the same clan, and share a childhood G.I. Joe stop-motion movie story.

segments.title: Modern ninja culture and the Iga Ninja Museum
segments.summary: They mention ninja in online culture, a pirate-versus-ninja rivalry, and the Ninja Museum and annual festival in Iga.

segments.title: Listener mail: geocaching and Santana CDs
segments.summary: A Columbus, Ohio geologist writes that a geocache contained Carlos Santana CDs, a result of the show's earlier geocaching episode, and another listener mentions a podcast inspired by the show.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close the episode and invite listener mail.
